paragraphs: Friend, this is a letter from a man near the end, and he's not wasting a single line. Paul tells Timothy to "Preach the word," and he says it in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead (2 Timothy 4:1-2). That means the Word isn't a hobby or a side dish. It's the main thing, and Paul says to be prepared "in season and out of season" (2 Timothy 4:2).

Here's the part that stings a little. Paul says a time will come when people "will not tolerate sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires" (2 Timothy 4:3). I think we all know that itch, baker. Nobody likes hearing the hard part, but the truth is still the truth when we skip it. So Paul says, "But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry" (2 Timothy 4:5). Whatever everybody else is chasing, stay with the Word.

And look where Paul's eyes go at the end. He says, "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7). Then he says the crown of righteousness is laid up for him, and "not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing" (2 Timothy 4:8). That's an open door, friend. Keep the Word close, keep running, and keep your eyes on the One who is coming.
